rules_evaluated.evidence: Strategy doc pins M1 mood as "Joyful creation — 'it works, on my repo'" (arc table M1 row; mood arc opens on it). The file frames exactly that and does not resolve or flatten it: the Big Idea at L6 is forward-leaning ('Your first session should leave something behind that the next one can use'), and the opening beat at L38 is a trick-share ('what's your favourite Claude Code trick that not many people know?') — celebratory, peer-register, no unease. Student leaves holding a PR, a closed ticket and a rules file born from their own session — 'it works, on my repo' — and L90 hands the next mood ('grounded competence') forward without pre-resolving it: 'Module 2 is where plan mode earns its keep'. Line closest to violating: L33 'Protect your working memory. Cut where needed. No need to read the agent's output word for word.' — flat, low-affect, but it is a room-agreement/pacing beat, i.e. a setup beat under the mood-floor carve-out (the student's job there is to get into position, not to learn), and it compresses to a parenthetical without breaking the arc. Mood-floor does not apply to it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: `sed -n '1,91p' getting-going.md | grep -nEi "hallucinat|fabricat|violation|failure mode|Remember:"` → ZERO hits (validated against a planted string: `printf 'hallucination test' | grep -nEi ...` → `1:hallucination test`, so the zero is real). Judgement, line closest to violating — L59: 'The agent's self-report is a hypothesis, not ground truth.' It names the hazard, but leads on the positive epistemic discipline (treat self-report as hypothesis, verify against the artifact) and never on a failure word; the negative case arrives as the second clause, which is exactly the shape §3 prescribes. Same for L6's Big Idea: discipline first ('should leave something behind that the next one can use'), failure case second ('Otherwise you have a clever assistant and no compounding'). All five What-You'll-Learn verbs are positive disciplines: Run / Distinguish / Fix / Close / Compound.

Four M1 sequencing claims pulled from the strategy doc and checked against the body. (a) 'No plan mode in M1 — M2 owns plan-mode-at-depth': honored twice — L18 '**Fix** the bug tests-first, root-cause-driven, no plan mode, and ship the PR', and L90 hands it downstream, 'Module 2 is where plan mode earns its keep'. (b) 'No Skill use at M1 — first Skill use, first subagent, first authoring all land together at M3': `grep -nEi "skill|subagent"` over the body returns only L83, inside the Cherny watch-pitch ('subagent map-reduce'), which the strategy doc explicitly licenses under M1's optional-read *Carries by inclusion:* list (parallel worktrees #2, subagent map-reduce #6) — a named item in someone else's talk, not a taught primitive. No Skill is installed, invoked or explained. (c) 'The loop is orient → fix → close → compound; do not reorder compound ahead of the close': L57 and L16 both print the order intact. (d) 'The progression page is a deliberate early encounter, not a spent reveal' — L79 pitches it as an orientation map, matching the doc. Line closest to violating: L71 'Sweep 100 resolved PR comments… find missing repository rules, and reject any proposed rule without three examples' — brushes M4's memory territory, but it sits under `## Optional challenges` `<!--tier:3-->` framed at L67 as 'a side quest before Module 2', so it front-runs no teaching moment; the exercise, the reveal and the module spine all still land at M4.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked all six Key Concepts bullets (L57–62) asking which theme each instances; five of six carry one, well above the 2–3 floor, each in module language rather than doc vocabulary. L57 'The loop is orient → fix → close → compound' → theme 2 (compounding builds the system). L58 '`/context` shows what landed in the window. What didn't land is real' → theme 1 (90% correct — the unread slice). L59 'The agent's self-report is a hypothesis… The scrollback is the machine's reflection' → themes 3+4 (mirror; mechanically self-aware, grain of salt — verify against the artifact). L61 'A `./CLAUDE.local.md` built from session evidence reads different from one drafted blank' → theme 2 again, first compound step. L62 'that tracker encodes conventions living in the tickets' → theme 5 (the agent capturing your world; conventions nobody wrote down). This matches the doc's own M1 plant list verbatim in intent (mirror / self-aware+salt / 90% / capture-your-world / compounding). Line closest to violating: L60 'A failing test is what makes the fix checkable. Without it, the fix is a guess that happens to compile' — the one tactical bullet with no theme behind it, which §6 explicitly permits ('keep tactical bullets as module's own voice, one idea each'); §5's floor is met five times over without it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section.
rules_evaluated.evidence: §§3/4/5 run first as gates: every bullet clears them (see rows 3, 4, 5), so no bullet is a decorated corpse. Shape: no `Remember:` label and no bold anywhere in the section — `grep -n 'Remember:'` over L54–62 → 0; the retired labelled+bolded form is absent, and I am scoring by reading the clause, not by scanning for a marker. Breadcrumb count = 3, inside the 1–3 range, each a compact memorable closing clause in engineer register: L58 'Context is what you put in it.' (5 words), L59 'The scrollback is the machine's reflection; current state lives on disk.' (mirror, essence not notation), L62 'One ticket is enough to start reading them back' (capture-your-world). No standalone **Themes this module instances:** section exists. Variety check against the adjacent module: `plan-mode-done-right.md`'s Key Concepts close on 'Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part.' and 'The skill is old; only the surface is new.' — different themes, no verbatim or near-verbatim repeat across the M1↔M2 window. Directional discipline holds: L58's breadcrumb names the move (what you put in the window), not a trust ratio.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus.
rules_evaluated.evidence: §§3/4 gates clear (rows 3, 4). Apparatus check, all four failure modes, mechanical over L16–20: no Bloom-tag parentheticals — `grep -nE '\((Analyze|Evaluate|Create|Understand|Apply|Remember)\)'` → 0 hits, Bloom level lives once in the maintainer Meta at L126; no 'by …ing' mechanism tails; no author-defence asides ('not a…'); no didactic taxonomy stamp (no ': the three things that…'). Register: strip each bullet to verb + object and it reads as work a peer would recognise — 'Run a loop on a trivial bug', 'Fix the bug tests-first', 'Close the bug's ticket', 'Compound the session into a rules file'. L20 '**Compound** the session into a personal rules file at `./CLAUDE.local.md`' is the §7 model shape exactly: practice leads, path is destination, not the inverted 'Sharpen ./CLAUDE.local.md with…' failure. L18's 'tests-first, root-cause-driven, no plan mode' is the carve-out (c) one-line operational how-to — the bullet is cryptic without it and it stays a single line. Line closest to violating — L17: '**Distinguish** the agent's account of your repo from the repo's actual state.' `Distinguish` is not one of AE101's theme verbs (Compound, Earn, Mirror, Ground, Introspect, Sharpen, Capture) and leans toward the Bloom-Analyze register §7 failure-mode (a) warns about. It stays inside because the object is concrete and named (the agent's account vs. the repo's actual state), the bullet describes work rather than something the curriculum does to the student, and four of the five bullets do lead on discipline verbs — §7 requires theme verbs to land across the training, not on every bullet. Filed as a todo, not a finding.

M1's deliberate mood is 'joyful creation' (strategy doc §237, §256), not 'unease' — this rule is explicitly scoped to unease-mood modules ('When mood is unease...'). No unease-framed language appears anywhere in the current body or in the pinned diff to test against either reading.

todos.note: L17 What-You'll-Learn bullet leads on **Distinguish** — an Analyze-taxonomy verb rather than one of AE101's strategic theme verbs. The bullet's content is the mirror / grain-of-salt theme (Claude's account vs. the repo's state), so a theme verb fits the grammar cleanly: **Mirror** the agent's account of your repo against its actual state, or **Ground** the agent's account of your repo in what's actually on disk. Non-blocking: register is correct and the object is concrete; this is a theme-recurrence upgrade, not a shape violation. Maintainer call — the current verb also matches the Meta block's stated Apply+Analyze Bloom level.
